minutes.headline: Select Board declined a School Choice Week proclamation and re-voted the police appointments to fix a procedural notice error.
minutes.summary: The board re-ratified four police appointments for procedural reasons, renewed one common victualler license, and discussed a requested School Choice Week proclamation, with most members declining to support it. Members raised future agenda items, heard capital planning and committee reports, and received the town manager's update on street lights, grants, a bridge bid and COVID facility closures.

what_happened.line: The Select Board re-voted three police appointments, with the same effective dates, to meet the requirement to notify the town clerk.
The board made no motion on the requested School Choice Week proclamation, so it will not be issued; most members declined to support it.
The board renewed one common victualler license and ratified a further full-time police officer appointment, with one member recused.
The chair is to re-sign the 300 Holman Street right-of-first-refusal waiver with per-lot wording; the total sale price is unchanged.
The town manager reported no brownfields grant for 925 Mass Ave, eight bids on the Pleasant Street bridge, and no bids on a West Street parcel.

why_it_matters: The Unitil street light purchase carries an asset value that can change until title transfer is recorded, so the final cost to the town budget, mostly taxes, is not yet fixed.
Capital requests from the DPW exceed what can likely be funded, so prioritising them before funding amounts are known shapes which road and equipment projects reach spring town meeting.
The bridge contract and the planned land transfers to conservation are items residents may be asked to weigh in on or vote on at town meeting.
watch_next: Next meeting January 5, with a workshop on the 12th with the APDC on the old primary school.
A presentation on planned land transfers to conservation ahead of spring town meeting, as requested.
